scope: Records the coordinated repair of all nine actionable CodeRabbit findings on the B550 cold-tier PR: the random session expression, selection stride, partial-group bound, asynchronous slot ownership and completion lifetime, acceptance identity parsing, artifact-hash parsing, and the durable identity wording. It does not compile CUDA or run a model.

checks.result: repository quality gate and whitespace check passed
the repaired std::random_device session-id expression compiles and executes on the host; full generate.cpp still requires a backend build

findings: The critical finding was real: std::random_device() constructed a temporary rather than calling the device, so generate.cpp did not compile. The expression now calls rd() twice and reserves zero.
The commit copy used last_t_ as the selection stride while the device matrix uses max_t_; cudaMemcpy2D now copies each layer's active rows with the correct source and destination strides.
Cold restore now stops at geometry.blocks, so an unaligned final group cannot write past the pinned host allocation.

Asynchronous reads reserve distinct L1 slots, failed or canceled reads release their reservations, explicit records survive a flush until waited on or replaced by an already-ready group, and engine publication flushes before reporting a host boundary.
The acceptance harness now requests lsblk TYPE and parses sha256sum's binary/text marker correctly; both had unit-test mocks that hid the real output shape.
non_claims: No CUDA backend was compiled and no model ran.
The pinned host allocation remains unreduced.
The separate one-hour async worker timed out with a hanging partial implementation and was not integrated; its timeout receipt is preserved by the CCR worker run directory.
